narrativeProgression.description: Discusses the challenges and intricacies of finding valuable shipwrecks.
Emphasizes the focus on valuable shipwrecks, particularly those containing gold or silver.
Discusses the logistical challenges of acquiring valuable items in the past, relying on ships to transport goods and funds.
Explains how shipwrecks can rewrite history and change people's lives due to the stories and artifacts they reveal.
Uses the example of a $250,000 shipment from 200 years ago being equivalent to $400-500 million today due to inflation, emphasizing the potential value of these discoveries.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Emphasizes the importance of challenging assumptions, embracing unexpected findings, and adapting to changing circumstances. Also underscores the vast, untapped potential of the oceans.

mood.description: Primarily engaging and humorous, with moments of excitement and reflection.

narrativeProgression.description: Shares personal anecdotes of significant shipwreck discoveries, emphasizing how they can rewrite history and challenge assumptions.
Introduces the story of 'The Victory' shipwreck, initially believed to have been run aground due to the captain's negligence.
Reveals their research proved the original assumption about 'The Victory' to be incorrect, highlighting how shipwrecks can rewrite history.
Discusses a shipwreck initially believed to be the 'Mercedes,' but turned out to be a different ship carrying valuable coins.
Shares the discovery of the yellow 'silver' bars that turned out to be silver with gold impurities, creating a humorous and exciting moment.
Recounts their 'biggest loss' - a ship carrying valuable coins that was claimed by Spain, despite containing private property, leading to their shift toward underwater mining.
Highlights the vast potential of the seas, revealing their discovery of bacteria that could lead to a new antibiotic.

scenes.title: Significant Discoveries and Historical Insights

youtube_description:
Meet Bradford Baker, one of the world most successful treasure hunters.  His company, Odyssey Marine Exploration, is publicly traded on the stock exchange — and has recovered hundreds of millions of dollars of sunken gold and silver.  Now, he sees intriguing possibilities that could be even more precious.

On September 20th, 2015, innovators in Technology, Entertainment, Design, and Entrepreneurship will gather for a one-day conference in Lower Manhattan, for a day of creative collaboration and cross-disciplinary inspiration. In this video, we interview one of the presenters, to give a sneak peek at what the event will be like.

This video was produced by Aaron Sylvan and edited by Tim Luangkhot, with camera work by Tim Luangkhot and audio by Denny Daniel.  Made in the offices of TEDxFultonStreet.
